stories.headline: DUTCH TO INTERN FORMER KAISER; Holland Embarrassed by His Presence--Officials Go to Confer with Him. REMAINS ON RAILWAY TRAIN Three More German Rulers Ousted--All the Rest Likely to Go. Said to Have Planned Internment. DUTCH TO INTERN FORMER KAISER
stories.summary: The Dutch government has decided to intern the former German Kaiser, who fled to Holland after the garrison in Liege revolted, and three other German rulers have been ousted, with the rest likely to follow. The Kaiser remains on a railway train as officials go to confer with him.

stories.headline: ARMIES VIEW EACH OTHER; Across Moselle Thousands of Enemy TroopsLoiter in Camps.TIME EXTENSION REFUSEDAmericans Veto a Request forDelayed Retiring Owing toFew Bridges.LUXEMBURG PEOPLE COOLERGerman Population at the Border Greet Pershing ForceLess Heartily. First View of Germany. ARMIES VIEW EACH OTHER American Officers in Troves. FOR RELEASED AMERICANS. Our Red Cross in France to Provide for Those Returning. GERMAN BARRIERS RAZED. Americans Destroy Steel and Concrete Obstacles Near Verdun. PERSHING GOES TO CHAUMONT His Special Train Drawn by an American Locomotive. RECORD OF 26TH DIVISION. New England Men Were in All Our Big Operations of the War. BRITISH ON GERMAN BORDER. Have Reached Frontier to the North of Luxemburg.
stories.summary: American and German armies are facing each other across the Moselle river, with thousands of enemy troops loitering in camps, as General Pershing's force is greeted less heartily by the German population at the border. The Americans have destroyed steel and concrete obstacles near Verdun.

stories.headline: SPEED SURRENDER UNDER NAVAL TRUCE; Allied and German Delegates Will Confer at a British Port Today. RODMAN AMERICAN ENVOY Crews of U-Boats Said to Have Decided to Oppose Revolution. RHODES ON MISSION TO SPA. General of Rainbow Division Starts Today for German Headquarters. SPEED SURRENDER UNDER NAVAL TRUCE WANTS A VOICE ON ISLANDS. Australia Asks to be Consulted About Pacific Bases. WILLING TO ACCOMMODATE. German Fleet Had Only to Come Out, Wemyss Told Truce Envoys. POPE WATCHING AUSTRIA. Prays for Just Settlement of Irredentist Problems. WILL FREE 420,000 FRENCH. German Headquarters Arranging the Details of Their Repatriation. British Labor Wants Voice on Peace BEGIN EUACUATING POLAND. Germans in Warsaw Disarmed-- Reports of Pogrom There. 'OUR LADY OF VICTORY.' People of Albert Say She Clung to Her Tower Till Foe Was Beaten.
stories.summary: Allied and German delegates will confer at a British port to discuss surrender under a naval truce, with Admiral Rodman as the American envoy, as crews of U-boats oppose the revolution and favor reinstating officers. Australia is asking to be consulted about Pacific bases.

stories.headline: MOONEY SENTENCE IS COMMUTED TO PRISON FOR LIFE; California Governor Saves from Gallows Labor Leader Convicted of Bomb Murder. CITES PRESIDETN'S ADVICE But Convict Issues Statement from Cell Protesting Against Living Death. LABOR IS NOT SATISFIED Leaders Say Mooney Should Have a New Trial to Establish Guilt or Innocence. Motives of Anarchism. President Wilson's Messages. MOONEY SENTENCE IS COMMUTED Labor Demands a New Trial. Will Carry Out Protest Strike. New York Leaders Not Satisfied. FIGHT TO SAVE MOONEY. Labor Made His Case Its Own, Both Here and Abroad. RED FLAG IN SAN FRANCISCO Several Members of the Bolshevist Group Rounded Up by Police.
stories.summary: President Wilson advised California Governor Stephens to commute the sentence of labor leader Tom Mooney, who was convicted of bomb murder, to life imprisonment, but Mooney and labor leaders are protesting and demanding a new trial to establish guilt or innocence.

rounds.blurb: The Dutch government interned the former German Kaiser, who had fled to Holland. German rulers were ousted and Allied forces faced the German army across the Moselle river. A naval truce led to surrender discussions between Allied and German delegates.

stories.headline: FREEDOM MARCH BEGINS AT SELMA; TROOPS ON GUARD; 3,200 Take Part in Protest as 54-Mile Rights Walk to Montgomery Starts DR. KING HAILS MISSION Envisions 'a New Alabama' and 'a New America' -- Crowd's Mood Festive 3,200 Begin Freedom March to Alabama's Capitol as Federal Troops Stand Guard A FESTIVE CROWD HEARS DR. KING He Envisions New Alabama and a New America -- Throng Is Heckled
stories.summary: Dr. King led a 54-mile civil rights march from Selma to Montgomery, with 3,200 participants and federal troops on guard, as he envisioned a new Alabama and a new America. The crowd's mood was festive despite being heckled.

stories.headline: U.S. TURNS DOWN THANT PROPOSAL ON TRUCE PARLEY; Says It Can Accept No Bid for a Vietnam Discussion Until 'Aggression' Ends CHANNELS REMAIN OPEN Hope Voiced for a Peaceful Solution -- Saigon Troops Score Major Victory U.S. TURNS DOWN THANT PROPOSAL
stories.summary: The US rejected a proposal by UN Secretary-General U Thant for a truce parley in Vietnam, stating that it would not accept an invitation to a conference until North Vietnamese aggression ended. The US remained open to a peaceful solution.

stories.headline: ALABAMA POLICE USE GAS AND CLUBS TO ROUT NEGROES; 57 Are Injured at Selma as Troopers Break Up Rights Walk in Montgomery DR. KING IS IN ATLANTA He Reveals Plans to Lead a New March Tomorrow -- Court Action Planned Alabama Police Use Gas and Clubs to Rout Negroes Attempting March on Capital 525 IN SELMA DEFY BAN OF GOVERNOR 17 Hospitalized as Officers Attack Demonstrators -- Dr. King in Atlanta
stories.summary: Alabama police used gas and clubs to break up a civil rights walk in Montgomery, injuring 57 people, while Dr. King planned to lead a new march the next day. The police also restrained newsmen during the clash.

stories.headline: JOHNSON URGES CONGRESS AT JOINT SESSION TO PASS LAW INSURING NEGRO VOTE; NATION HEARS HIM President, in TV Talk, Pledges That 'We Shall Overcome' Johnson Urges Congress at Joint Session to Pass Law Insuring Negro Voting Rights TV APPEAL CALLS FOR ACTION NOW Nation Hears President Say 'We Shall Overcome' in the War on Bigotry
stories.summary: President Lyndon B. Johnson urged Congress to pass a law ensuring Negro voting rights, pledging that 'we shall overcome' in the war on bigotry, and calling for immediate action to abolish discriminatory voter qualification devices.

rounds.blurb: The Selma to Montgomery civil rights march began, led by Dr. King, with 3,200 participants and federal troops on guard. Dr. King envisioned a new Alabama and a new America. The US rejected a proposal for a truce parley in Vietnam.

stories.headline: MAY MAKE REFUND TO LIQUOR OWNERS; Prohibitionists Said to Approve Plan to Take Over Stock and Give Compensation. NO COST TO THE TREASURY Scheme Contemplates Sales from Warehouses for Industry--Supervisors Named. Many Thefts from Warehouses. MAY MAKE REFUND TO LIQUOR OWNERS Government Machinery Completed.
stories.summary: The US government is considering a plan to compensate liquor owners for their stock and take it over for sale under the law for non-beverage purposes, as Prohibition has led to many thefts from warehouses. This plan is being developed during a time of significant social change in the United States.

stories.headline: FOES OF TREATY HOLD UP PARLEY; THREATEN LODGE; Bitter-Enders Block Conference at Which It Was Hoped to Agree on Article X. HOLD MEETING OF PROTEST Johnson and Borah Hint Revolt on Leader--Sherman Talks of Bolt from Party. FEAR COLLAPSE OF PARLEYS Taft Confers with Mild Group-- Ashurst Assails Nursing of Presidential Booms.
stories.summary: Republican senators are blocking a treaty compromise, potentially damaging the process beyond repair, with some threatening to revolt against their leader, as the US navigates the aftermath of World War I. Senators Johnson and Borah are key figures in this opposition.

stories.headline: SOCIALISTS ELATED; SEE PROPAGANDA IN ASSEMBLY'S ACT; Excluded Members Raised from a Harmless Minority to a Political Force, Says One. PREPARE APPEAL TO LABOR Issue Statement Declaring Lusk Committee Feared Possible Disclosures. SUBMIT LIST OF QUESTIONS Public Men Differ as to Assembly's Attitude--Craig Approves; Hylan Demurs.
stories.summary: Socialist leaders are preparing to defend themselves before the Assembly Judiciary Committee after being excluded from the State Assembly, with some seeing this as an opportunity to gain propaganda and build support, during a time of heightened political tension in the US.

stories.headline: FLETCHER RESIGNS AS AMBASSADOR IN MEXICO CITY; Our Envoy Said to Feel It Is Impossible for Him to Deal Further with Carranza.--HAS PRESSED OUR DEMANDS-- Many Disputes with Carranza Have Robbed His Mission of Future Usefulness.--RECENTLY IN WASHINGTON-- His Service in Mexico Covered the Period of German Intrigue and Border Troubles.
stories.summary: Henry P. Fletcher has resigned as US Ambassador to Mexico, citing the impossibility of dealing with the Mexican government and the loss of usefulness of his mission, following many disputes with Carranza, as the US navigates complex international relations in the region.

rounds.blurb: Prohibition enforcement led to a proposed plan to compensate liquor owners for their stock. The US government considered taking over liquor stock for industrial sales. Republican senators blocked a treaty compromise, threatening to revolt against their leader.
